correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all-degree proof: on each 2d-point circle the discrete Fourier transform of the real intensity difference annihilates harmonics |k|<d and leaves only collision ±d. Its coefficient is R^d(a_d conjugate(a_0)−b_d conjugate(b_0)); the two independent real projections force this common complex number to zero exactly when sin(d(psi−phi))≠0. Thus continuous moduli coincide on both distinct circles; the nonzero rational quotient f/g is invariant under positive nonunit dilation of its conjugate reflection and must be constant by its Laurent series, with modulus one. Zero-polynomial and vanishing endpoint coefficient cases are included. If r=s, f=z and g=r witness ambiguity; if the sine vanishes, 1±i exp(−id phi)z^d witness ambiguity. The normalized top-bin real 2x2 matrix has singular values sqrt(1±|cos(d(psi−phi))|), giving the exact optimal staggering. Independently reconstructed Git tree from seven actual blob identities; separate checker corroborated 3081 finite Fourier, ambiguity and singular-value comparisons over d=1..13. Finite comparisons do not establish the universal quantifier.

value.rationale: Structured finite evaluation of a degree-at-most-d polynomial from modulus-only measurements is a naturally motivated phase-retrieval problem; fixing exactly equal 2d/2d regular polygons gives an entire, simple geometric family with nontrivial sharp success and failure geometry. The theorem provides a complete all-degree if-and-only-if, explicit ambiguity witnesses, reconstructs both intensity Fourier polynomials from samples, and characterizes optimally conditioned angular top-harmonic demixing, beyond a fixed small-degree experiment or arbitrary slice. It does not purport to establish general nonlinear noise stability or globally optimal sample cardinality.

final_claim: For every d≥1 and r,s>0, two concentric regular 2d-gon intensity sample sets determine all complex polynomials of degree≤d up to global phase iff r≠s and sin(d(psi−phi))≠0. Each continuous circle intensity is then recovered by finite DFT and the top-harmonic 2x2 system has singular values sqrt(1±|cos(d(psi−phi))|).
